package_info.package_manager: AWS/EKS (cloud platform feature, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Kubernetes 1.23+ with EKS platform version as per cluster (see table in report)
package_info.why_malicious: The report does not describe a malicious package, but rather highlights how the new EKS Cluster Access Management feature can be abused by attackers to escalate privileges, gain unauthorized access, or persist administrative access to EKS clusters. The risk lies in the misuse of legitimate API operations (such as CreateAccessEntry and AssociateAccessPolicy) to grant excessive or cross-account access, not in a specific malicious code package.

execution_context.file_location: N/A (executed as AWS API call, not in a file)
required_permissions: AWS IAM permissions to call eks:CreateAccessEntry

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates a new access entry for a specified AWS principal on an EKS cluster, enabling that principal to be granted Kubernetes permissions, resulting in potential privilege escalation or unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This operation can be abused by attackers with sufficient AWS permissions to grant themselves or others access to EKS clusters, bypassing existing access controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, access entries should only be created by trusted administrators for legitimate users. Malicious use involves creating entries for attacker-controlled principals.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate administrators use this to onboard new team members or service accounts.
key_indicators: Creation of access entries for unexpected or external principals
Bulk creation of access entries in a short time

execution_context.file_location: N/A (executed as AWS API call, not in a file)
required_permissions: AWS IAM permissions to call eks:AssociateAccessPolicy

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code associates a highly privileged managed access policy (e.g., AmazonEKSAdminPolicy) to a principal's access entry, granting them administrator-level permissions on the EKS cluster.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Attackers can use this to escalate privileges by assigning themselves or others admin-level access to the cluster.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, admin policies are only assigned to trusted roles. Malicious use involves unauthorized assignment to attacker-controlled roles.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cluster administrators may assign admin policies during legitimate onboarding.
key_indicators: Assignment of AmazonEKSAdminPolicy or AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy to unexpected principals
Assignment of admin policies in bulk or to external accounts

execution_context.file_location: N/A (executed as AWS API call, not in a file)
required_permissions: AWS IAM permissions to call eks:CreateAccessEntry

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates an access entry for a principal and maps them to a custom Kubernetes group, potentially granting granular or unexpected permissions within the cluster.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Attackers may use this to grant themselves or others access to sensitive resources by mapping to powerful Kubernetes groups.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, group mappings are carefully managed. Malicious use involves mapping attacker-controlled roles to privileged groups.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Used by admins to grant granular access to specific users.
key_indicators: Mapping of attacker-controlled roles to privileged or sensitive Kubernetes groups
Unusual group names or bulk group assignments

execution_context.file_location: N/A (executed as AWS API call, not in a file)
required_permissions: AWS IAM permissions to call eks:DeleteAccessEntry

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code deletes an access entry for a principal, removing their access to the EKS cluster, which can be used to cover tracks or disrupt legitimate access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Attackers may remove legitimate administrators or evidence of their own access to evade detection or maintain exclusive control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, access removal is part of offboarding. Malicious use involves removing legitimate users or hiding attacker access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Used by admins to remove access for departing users.
key_indicators: Deletion of access entries for legitimate admin/service roles
Access entry deletion immediately after privilege escalation

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates access entries for their own or external AWS principals on one or more EKS clusters.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to assign permissions or policies to these principals.

attack_chain.action: Attacker associates highly privileged managed access policies (e.g., AmazonEKSAdminPolicy) or sensitive Kubernetes groups to their access entries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains admin or granular access to the EKS cluster.

attack_chain.action: Attacker optionally deletes access entries for legitimate administrators to maintain exclusive control or cover their tracks.

behavioral_signatures: Creation of access entries (CreateAccessEntry) for unexpected or external principals
Association of admin-level managed access policies (AmazonEKSAdminPolicy, AmazonEKSClusterAdminPolicy) to new or suspicious principals
Bulk granting of access to multiple clusters in a short time
Deletion of access entries for legitimate admin/service roles
file_indicators: No direct file indicators (actions are API-driven), but changes to aws-auth ConfigMap or sudden absence of expected entries may be suspicious
network_indicators: CloudTrail events for eks.amazonaws.com with eventNames: CreateAccessEntry, AssociateAccessPolicy, UpdateAccessEntry, DeleteAccessEntry
Unusual principalArn values (external accounts, attacker-controlled roles)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CloudTrail for CreateAccessEntry, AssociateAccessPolicy, and DeleteAccessEntry events on EKS clusters. Alert on assignment of admin-level policies to unexpected principals, creation of access entries for external or new principals, and deletion of access entries for legitimate users. Aggregate by principalArn and clusterName to detect bulk or cross-account access grants. Correlate with changes to the aws-auth ConfigMap if still in use.
